fit: shared sublingual olive oil and composite Parkinson mobility
assessment: The between-arm timed-up-and-go estimate was 0.49 seconds (95% CI −1.08 to 2.06). Both arms used the same olive-oil carrier. The paper gives no separate balance item, cold-pressed grade or independent oil effect.

fit: shared olive-oil cannabis vehicle and baseline motor symptoms
assessment: Postural instability appears among six participants' baseline features. Serial balance outcomes and a plain-oil group are absent. The study assigns two active doses and gives no oil grade.

fit: shared sublingual olive oil and composite Parkinson motor outcome
assessment: The adjusted UPDRS III difference for the randomized cannabinoid comparison was 1.28 points (95% CI −3.86 to 6.41). The article reports no individual rest-tremor item or oil-specific estimate.

fit: common olive vehicle and baseline tremor
assessment: Baseline clinical features include tremor. The six-person series does not give change in rest tremor or processing grade. Both active-dose groups use a common carrier.

fit: shared sublingual olive oil and composite motor score
assessment: The overall UPDRS III comparison was inconclusive. No bradykinesia item estimate or oil grade was published. The contrast estimates adding cannabinoid extract to a common olive-oil vehicle.
Baseline features include bradykinesia. Serial bradykinesia and a cold-pressed olive-oil-only comparator were unmeasured across the two cannabinoid doses.

fit: oral peanut-oil oleogel placebo and BDI-II in irritable bowel syndrome
assessment: The control group mean changed from 11.02 at baseline to 10.20 at week four and 10.11 at follow-up. The comparison assigns anise preparations and gives no plain-oil contrast, refining grade or Parkinson population.

fit: oral arachis-oil placebo and depression in low vitamin D
assessment: Mean BDI-II change was −1.9 in the placebo arm and −1.5 in the vitamin D arm with inconclusive adjustment. The placebo formulation identifies arachis oil. Its dose and grade and the active vehicle are unverified.

fit: topical and inhaled peanut-oil comparator and HADS depression
assessment: The peanut-only arm mean fell from 6.92 to 5.54. Both randomized arms used the oil. Route, non-Parkinson population and unclear analysis denominators prevent transfer to refined culinary oil.

fit: developmental mouse diets with peanut oil and three anxiety proxies
assessment: Total dietary oil was matched but peanut/rapeseed proportions and alpha-linolenic acid differed. All three anxiety assays were inconclusive. The study could not isolate cold-pressed oil in human Parkinson disease.

fit: topical peanut-oil control and acute mood measurements
assessment: The journal abstract gives no clinical anxiety estimate. A probably related thesis measured acute calm/restlessness and compared topical clary-sage mixture with a shared peanut vehicle. The clinical disorder, oral route and independent exposure were not studied.

fit: topical and inhaled peanut-oil comparator and HADS anxiety
assessment: The peanut-only group mean changed from 11.18 to 8.63. Both groups received peanut oil in topical/inhalational care, with no grade or independent unexposed comparison and inconsistent participant flow details.

fit: shared ungraded olive carrier and insomnia severity in a two-dose case series
assessment: The three-person higher-dose group had a within-group ISI change at day 60 (p=.03). The cohort compares two active cannabis doses in olive oil, without olive-only or olive-free group, so the association cannot identify oil direction.
